# Huy Tran

> Senior Software Engineer / Product Engineer. Systems-minded builder:
> architecture, implementation, verification, release — with the evidence
> attached. Based in Vietnam, working remote.

Canonical: https://huypkc.github.io/

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/huypkc

## Positioning

Ten years of frontend and product work — FPT Software, GO1, CyberLogitec, and
CBTW APAC since 2022 — now working across the whole line rather than one layer
of it: why → system → architecture → implementation → proof.

The working principle is on the site in one sentence: **claim only what
survives verification**. Every number below is one a gate produces, not an
estimate.

## Capabilities

- Product engineering and system architecture
- API contracts as OpenAPI, gated in CI so the spec and the implementation
  cannot drift apart silently
- Reliability engineering, security boundaries, threat-model-led design
- CI/CD and release engineering, including signed Android artifacts
- Flutter and Dart (mobile)
- TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js (web)
- Firebase, Supabase
- Local-first software — data that stays on the device

## Open to

Senior and founding engineering roles. Product infrastructure. Backend
architecture. Mobile platform and release. Reliability and security.
Distributed and real-time systems. Remote, contract, or founding-team
collaboration.

Stated plainly so a machine does not have to infer it: distributed and
real-time systems is a direction of interest, **not** a claim of prior
production experience. There is no shipped RTB, HFT, high-event-throughput or
sub-100ms latency work behind that line.

## Evidence

- **One Frame** — a private, local-first photo journal for Android. One
  photograph and one sentence a day, encrypted before it touches disk, proven
  by reading the bytes back. 220 Flutter tests. A signed v2 Android artifact.
  Verified on device, in release validation, not published to any store.
  https://huypkc.github.io/one-frame.html
- **ThunViet V2** — contract-first delivery: requirement → authorise → isolate
  → build → verify → release. 638 TypeScript tests, 14 contract operations
  verified.

Counts are the output of a run, not an estimate: `flutter test` and
`node --test`, both executed 2026-08-29.

What is deliberately not claimed: no Play Store listing, no store release, no
production users, no uptime figure, no iOS build, no TestFlight.

## Timeline

https://huypkc.github.io/timeline is a dated record of how my engineering
decisions changed while building these systems, August 2026 onward. The unit is
a thought, not a commit: an entry exists because something was thought on a
date about real work, and evidence is attached underneath when it exists.

Entries are never rewritten when a later one contradicts them. The original
stays in its own words and links to what replaced it, so the page shows the
revisions as well as the conclusions. Statuses are HYPOTHESIS, SUPPORTED,
APPLIED, VERIFIED, REVISED and SUPERSEDED, and they are not decoration: only a
narrow claim with directly inspectable evidence is VERIFIED, and where the
origin of a thought cannot be established the entry says so rather than
inventing a date.

## Evidence appendix

https://huypkc.github.io/evidence.html names each command behind the numbers,
where and at which commit it ran, and links the unedited output committed
beside the page. Four of the six runs are from private repositories, so a
reader can see what was printed but cannot re-run it; the page says so rather
than implying otherwise. Read access for review is available on request.
